QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_11

question.text: A trader buys 10 lots of bond futures at Rs. 99.00 in the morning and sells 6 lots at Rs. 99.40 in the afternoon. The DSP is Rs. 99.30. Lot size is 2,000. What is the total MTM settlement?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per pages 240 and 255-256 of the NISM Series IV workbook, all positions including intraday closed positions are marked to the daily settlement price using weighted-average trade prices. Intraday closed 6 lots: (99.40 - 99.00) x 2,000 x 6 = Rs. 4,800 profit. Remaining 4 open long lots: (99.30 - 99.00) x 2,000 x 4 = Rs. 2,400 profit. Total MTM = 4,800 + 2,400 = Rs. 7,200. The Trap: Rs. 6,000 only considers the buy side at DSP for all 10 lots and ignores the closed-leg profit captured at the actual sell price. Rs. 5,400 and Rs. 3,600 reflect incorrect netting against DSP for the closed leg. The source-backed method splits closed-vs-open and applies trade-vs-DSP and DSP-vs-prior-day to each correctly. Note: Per page 255, intraday closed futures profit/loss is based on weighted-average prices; per page 240, every position (intraday and open) is marked to the DSP.
